descriptors.definition: An entity must provide reconciliations of reportable segments' totals for revenues, profit or loss, assets, liabilities, and other material items to the corresponding entity amounts. All material reconciling items must be separately identified and described.
inclusion: Reconciliation of total segment revenues to entity revenues
Reconciliation of total segment profit or loss to entity profit or loss before tax
Reconciliation of segment assets and liabilities if reported
exclusion: Disclosed segment amounts without entity-level totals
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from segment revenue measurement because it bridges internal segment measures to external entity financial statements.

descriptors.definition: If an entity changes its internal organizational structure causing reportable segment composition to change, corresponding prior period information must be restated unless information is unavailable and development costs are excessive. When prior period information is not restated, current period segment information must be reported on both old and new bases.
inclusion: Restatement of interim and annual corresponding prior period data
Dual reporting on old and new bases when restatement is impracticable due to excessive cost
exclusion: Changes in accounting estimates without structural organization changes
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard prospective application by mandating dual-basis reporting for the change year if historical restatement is excessively costly.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide entity-wide disclosures regarding products, services, geographical areas, and major customers regardless of how their operating segments are organized. These additional disclosures use financial information utilized to produce the entity's financial statements.
inclusion: Revenues from external customers for products and services
Geographical revenue and non-current asset disclosures
exclusion: Information already reported directly as part of segment reporting requirements under the standard
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard segment disclosures because they apply universally across the entity regardless of the internal management approach used to identify operating segments.

descriptors.definition: An entity should report revenues from external customers for each product and service or group of similar products and services based on financial statement data. Disclosure is excused only if necessary information is unavailable and development costs are excessive.
inclusion: Revenues for individual products and services
Revenues for groups of similar products and services
nearby_distinctions: Differs from geographical disclosures by focusing on product lines rather than physical or regional customer locations.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose external customer revenues and non-current assets attributed to the country of domicile and individual foreign countries, stating the attribution basis used. Material individual foreign country amounts must be presented separately from totals.
inclusion: Revenues attributed to domicile and foreign countries
Non-current assets located in domicile and foreign countries
exclusion: Financial instruments, deferred tax assets, post-employment benefit assets, and insurance rights from non-current asset totals
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from product disclosures by segregating metrics based on geographic locations of customers and asset holdings.

descriptors.definition: An entity must disclose its reliance on major customers if revenues from a single external customer reach or exceed ten percent of total revenues. Common control groups constitute a single customer, while government-controlled entities require judgment regarding economic integration.
inclusion: Disclosure of the fact of dependence when 10% threshold is met
Total amount of revenues from each such customer
Identity of the segment reporting the revenues
exclusion: Disclosure of the specific identity of the major customer
Breakdown of revenues each segment earns from that customer
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard segment revenue reporting by establishing specific customer-concentration disclosure thresholds at the entity level.

descriptors.concept_name: Significant Differences In Ind As 108 Vis-A-Vis As 17
descriptors.definition: Ind AS 108 adopts a management approach for identifying segments based on internal reports reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, contrasting with AS 17 which relies on primary and secondary risks and returns. Furthermore, Ind AS 108 measures amounts based on management resource allocation and performance evaluation rather than strict accounting policy conformity.
inclusion: Comparison of aggregation criteria and single-segment disclosures
exclusion: Detailed procedural instructions for AS 17 application
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts current management-driven segment identification with older accounting standard frameworks that forced primary and secondary business versus geographical categorizations.
